topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Origins and Drivers of Cancer: Genetic Predisposition, Endogenous Processes, and Environmental Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic genetic factors, endogenous cellular processes, and extrinsic environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, dietary, chemical, and physical agents alongside the cellular and tissue-level mechanisms by which initiators and promoters drive malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify mutational signatures and determine whether substances are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section provides final framing and concluding reflections on evaluating carcinogenic risk versus practical benefits in daily life.
